zh.principle: **协议**：DTLS 1.0（DTLS 1.0）。摘要界定版本与对象：「This document specifies Version 1.0 of the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol.The DTLS protocol provides communications privacy for datagram protocols.」即在不保证顺序与交付的传输上提供 TLS 级保护，并保留数据报语义。
zh.why: 设计取向是最小改动：§1 写明「DTLS is deliberately designed to be as similar to TLS as possible, both to minimize new security invention and to maximize the amount of code and infrastructure reuse.」§4 说明写法：「instead of presenting DTLS as a new protocol, we present it as a series of deltas from TLS 1.1 [TLS11].」
zh.used: §4.2 列出相对 TLS 的三处改动，第一条是「A stateless cookie exchange has been added to prevent denial of service attacks.」，随后是握手头的分片与乱序处理和重传计时器。§4.1.1 另给出一条硬性约束：「Each DTLS record MUST fit within a single datagram.」
zh.broken: 重放检测是可选的：§3.3 说明「The replay detection feature is optional, since packet duplication is not always malicious, but can also occur due to routing errors.」§4.1.2.2 直接禁掉流密码：「RC4 MUST NOT be used with DTLS.」cookie 只解决伪造源地址，§4.2.1 自陈「This mechanism does not provide any defense against DoS attacks mounted from valid IP addresses.」

en.principle: **Protocol**: DTLS 1.0 (DTLS 1.0). The abstract fixes version and object: "This document specifies Version 1.0 of the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol. The DTLS protocol provides communications privacy for datagram protocols." — TLS-level protection over a transport that guarantees neither order nor delivery, preserving datagram semantics.
en.why: The design aims at minimal change: §1 says "DTLS is deliberately designed to be as similar to TLS as possible, both to minimize new security invention and to maximize the amount of code and infrastructure reuse." Section 4 explains the presentation: "instead of presenting DTLS as a new protocol, we present it as a series of deltas from TLS 1.1 [TLS11]."
en.used:
Section 4.2 lists the three departures from TLS, first "A stateless cookie exchange has been added to prevent denial of service attacks.", then handshake-header changes for loss, reordering and fragmentation, plus retransmission timers. Section 4.1.1 adds a hard rule: "Each DTLS record MUST fit within a single datagram."

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: Replay detection is optional: §3.3 explains "The replay detection feature is optional, since packet duplication is not always malicious, but can also occur due to routing errors." Section 4.1.2.2 bans stream ciphers outright: "RC4 MUST NOT be used with DTLS." And the cookie answers only forged source addresses — §4.2.1 concedes "This mechanism does not provide any defense against DoS attacks mounted from valid IP addresses."
en.history: The RFC 4347 header lists E. Rescorla (RTFM, Inc.) and N. Modadugu (Stanford University), Category: Standards Track, April 2006, with no Obsoletes or Updates line; the title line reads only "Datagram Transport Layer Security" and the version number appears in the abstract.

zh: cookie 交换：无状态的源地址可达性验证。
HelloVerifyRequest：承载 cookie 的握手消息。
显式序号：记录头里的序号以便正确验证 MAC。
重传计时器：处理握手丢包的机制。
RC4 禁用：§4.1.2.2 的 MUST NOT。
en: Cookie exchange: a stateless return-routability check.
HelloVerifyRequest: the handshake message carrying the cookie.
Explicit sequence number: in the record header so the MAC verifies under reordering.
Epoch: separates records of successive handshakes.
Retransmission timers: the handshake answer to packet loss.
